newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer sets FIM 30 K-shr redemption price.
newsitem.headline: Amer sets FIM 30 K-shr redemption price.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy on Tuesday set a redemption price for its K-series shares of 30 markka each, and is offering new A shares for 20 markka each, but only to those institutions which hold K-shares.

For technical reasons the K shares are being redeemed and the A shares issued at prices well below their intrinsic values, but the exchange ratio of 1-to 1.5 keeps the financial interests of K share holders unchanged, except they will have more liquid shares.

"It is justified in setting the redemption price and subscription price for the issuance of the new A shares, respectively, as low as possible to protect the company's balance sheet and unrestricted equity," Amer said.
This was why the lowest possible price, or the A share's nominal price, was taken as the subscription price, it said.
"The K shares on the other hand are being redeemed for 30 markka per share, which is considerably below their current value," Amer said.
On Tuesday, Amer said it had redeemed 275,000 K shares offered to a British investor by one of four domestic institutional owners controlling its vote-strong K series for 273.64 markka per share.

As bourse trading in Amer's listed A share resumed after a suspension pending the announcement of the redemption and proposed conversion of K shares into A shares at a 1:1.5 ratio, the A share surged 8.2 percent or 7.50 markka to 98.80 markka.
Amer listed the following A- and K-share ownerships after the July 29 redemption:
Series A Series K
The Finnish Association
of Graduate Engineers 99,956 676,824
The Finnish Association of
Graduates of the Schools of

The Land and Water Technology Foundation 276,583 318,504

After conversion, the graduate engineers would control 4.6 percent of shares and votes, the economics and business school graduates 3.9 percent, the land and water technology foundation 3.1 percent and the business school's student union 2.1 percent, Amer said.

Nominee registrations -- all class A shares, which after the redemption accounted for 7.9 percent of votes and 64.6 percent of shares, would after the conversion have 62.4 percent of shares and votes.
